story: In the traditional account, a long flood struck the Yellow River plain in the time of the sage kings Yao and Shun. Yu's father Gun tried to hold the water back with dykes and failed. Yu instead dug channels to lead the water to the sea. He is said to have worked for thirteen years and passed his own door three times without going in.

Shun rewarded Yu by naming him successor. When Yu died, the lords followed his son Qi rather than the chosen minister Yi, and the throne became hereditary. Later historians count this as the start of the Xia, the first dynasty.

No writing from this time survives. The story comes from much later texts such as the Book of Documents and the Records of the Grand Historian, so most modern historians treat Yu as a figure of legend.
story_zh: 据传统说法，尧舜时代黄河流域洪水泛滥，久久不退。禹的父亲鲧用筑堤堵水的办法，没有成功。禹改用疏导，开挖河道，把洪水引入大海。相传他在外奔波十三年，三次经过家门都没有进去。
舜因此选定禹为继承人。禹死后，诸侯没有拥戴他指定的伯益，而是拥戴禹的儿子启，王位从此在一家之内世代相传。后世史家把这看作第一个王朝——夏朝的开端。
这一时期没有留下任何文字。上述故事出自晚得多的《尚书》《史记》等书，所以现代史学家大多把禹视为传说人物。
yu-founds-xia.why: The story marks the shift from choosing the worthiest ruler to passing power within one family, the pattern every later dynasty followed.
yu-founds-xia.why_zh: 这个故事标志着从“选贤”到“传子”的转变，此后历代王朝都沿用了家族世袭的模式。

people.name: Yu the Great
people.role: Flood tamer and founder of the Xia

people.name: Gun
people.role: Yu's father, who failed to stop the flood

quote.zh: 居外十三年，过家门不敢入。
quote.en: He lived away from home for thirteen years, and when he passed his own door he did not dare go in.
quote.from: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Xia 史记·夏本纪

story: In 1959 the historian Xu Xusheng toured western Henan looking for traces of the Xia. Near the village of Erlitou in Yanshi he found a large ancient site, and digging has gone on there ever since.

The site covers about three square kilometres. It has a walled palace area with large rammed-earth halls, the earliest known grid of roads in China, and workshops that cast bronze and worked turquoise. Here archaeologists found the oldest Chinese bronze ritual vessels, such as wine cups called jue, and a dragon figure made from about two thousand pieces of turquoise.

Erlitou was the largest centre of its day in the Yellow River valley. Its date and location match the late Xia of the traditional histories, but no writing has been found to prove which people lived there.
story_zh: 1959年，史学家徐旭生到豫西一带调查“夏墟”，在偃师二里头村附近发现了一处大型古代遗址，此后这里的发掘一直没有中断。
遗址面积约3平方公里，有带围墙的宫殿区和大型夯土建筑，有中国已知最早的网格状道路，还有铸铜和加工绿松石的作坊。这里出土了中国最早的青铜礼器，如被称为“爵”的酒器，以及一件用约两千片绿松石拼成的龙形器。
二里头是当时黄河流域规模最大的中心。它的年代和位置都与史书中的夏代晚期相符，但由于没有发现文字，住在这里的究竟是什么人仍无定论。
erlitou.why: Erlitou shows that a state-like society with palaces and bronze casting existed before the Shang, and it is the focus of the debate over whether the Xia was real.
erlitou.why_zh: 二里头证明，早在商代之前就已出现拥有宫殿和青铜铸造的国家形态社会，它也是“夏朝是否存在”这一争论的焦点。

people.name: Xu Xusheng
people.role: Historian who found the site in 1959

story: Shimao lies in Shenmu county in the far north of Shaanxi, on hills above a branch of the Yellow River. Local people had long seen stone walls there, but large-scale digging began only in 2011.

The city covers more than four square kilometres. An inner citadel sits on a terraced platform about 70 metres high, faced with stone. Two rings of stone walls, with gates, bastions and towers, surround it. Diggers found carved stone faces set into the walls, jade pieces pushed into the masonry, and pits with the skulls of dozens of young people, probably killed in rituals when the gate was built.
Shimao flourished from about 2300 to 1800 BCE, at the same time as the traditional Xia. It shows that large, powerful centres existed far to the north of the Central Plain.
story_zh: 石峁遗址位于陕西最北端的神木市，坐落在黄河支流旁的山梁上。当地人很早就见过这里的石墙，但大规模发掘直到2011年才开始。
古城面积超过400万平方米。核心是“皇城台”，这是一座高约70米、四周用石块包砌的阶梯状台城，外面还有内外两重石城墙，设有城门、马面和墩台。考古人员在墙上发现了石雕人面像和嵌在石缝里的玉器，还在城门附近发现了埋有数十个年轻人头骨的祭祀坑，很可能是筑城时举行仪式所杀。
石峁大约兴盛于公元前2300年至前1800年，与传说中的夏代同时。它说明在中原以北很远的地方，也曾存在强大的大型中心。
shimao-stone-city.why: Shimao shows that Chinese civilisation did not grow from a single centre on the Central Plain; several regions developed complex societies at the same time.
shimao-stone-city.why_zh: 石峁表明中华文明并非只从中原一个中心生长出来，多个地区同时发展出了复杂社会。

story: According to the traditional histories, Yu had chosen his minister Yi as successor. After Yu died, the lords went to Yu's son Qi instead, and Qi became king. This ended the old custom of passing rule to the most capable man.

Not everyone accepted the change. The Youhu clan, said to be related to the Xia royal house, refused to submit. Qi led his army against them, and the two sides met at Gan. Before the battle Qi gave a speech to his troops, preserved as the 'Speech at Gan' in the Book of Documents. He promised rewards for those who obeyed and death for those who did not.
Qi won and destroyed the Youhu. The location of Gan is uncertain; old commentators place it near Hu county, south-west of today's Xi'an.
story_zh: 据传统史书记载，禹生前选定大臣伯益为继承人。禹死后，诸侯却去拥戴禹的儿子启，启于是即位为王，传贤的旧习从此终结。
并不是所有部族都接受这一变化。据说与夏王室同姓的有扈氏拒不服从。启率军讨伐，双方在甘地交战。战前启向将士发表誓词，这就是《尚书》中的《甘誓》：服从命令的有赏，违抗命令的处死。
启最终获胜，灭掉了有扈氏。甘的具体位置并不确定，古代注家多认为在户县（今西安鄠邑区）一带。
qi-battle-of-gan.why: The victory confirmed that the throne would pass from father to son, the core rule of every later Chinese dynasty.
qi-battle-of-gan.why_zh: 这场胜利确立了父死子继的王位制度，这也是后世历代王朝的核心原则。

people.name: Qi
people.role: Son of Yu, king of Xia

people.name: Youhu clan
people.role: Clan that refused to accept Qi

quote.zh: 用命，赏于祖；弗用命，戮于社。
quote.en: Those who obey orders will be rewarded before the ancestors; those who disobey will be put to death before the altar of the soil.
quote.from: Book of Documents, Speech at Gan 尚书·甘誓

story: Lajia is a village site of the Qijia culture on the Yellow River in Minhe county, Qinghai. Around 2000 BCE a strong earthquake struck, followed by mudflows and floods that buried the houses.

When archaeologists dug the site in the early 2000s, they found people who had died inside their cave-like homes. In one house a woman knelt with a small child in her arms, as if trying to shield it. In 2005 scientists reported a sealed bowl from the site holding thin yellow noodles made from millet, the oldest noodles yet found.
Some researchers have linked the floods in this area to the legend of Yu's great flood, but that idea is still debated.
story_zh: 喇家遗址是齐家文化的一处村落，位于青海民和县的黄河岸边。大约公元前2000年，这里发生了强烈地震，接着泥石流和洪水掩埋了房屋。
21世纪初考古人员发掘时，在窑洞式的房屋里发现了当场遇难的人。其中一座房子里，一位妇女跪在地上，怀里紧抱着一个孩子，似乎想用身体护住他。2005年，研究人员公布了在遗址中发现的一只倒扣的碗，碗里是用小米做的细面条，这是迄今发现最古老的面条。
有学者认为这一带的洪水与大禹治水的传说有关，不过这个观点仍有争议。
lajia-disaster.why: Lajia gives a rare, direct picture of daily life and sudden disaster in the age of the traditional Xia.
lajia-disaster.why_zh: 喇家遗址为传说中夏代的日常生活和突发灾难提供了难得的直接画面。

story: The traditional histories say the Xia nearly fell early on. Qi's son Taikang cared only for hunting. While he was away across the Luo River, Yi, the chief of the Youqiong people and a famous archer, blocked his return and took control.

Yi was later killed by his own follower Han Zhuo, who seized power and hunted down the Xia royal line. A pregnant Xia queen escaped to her own clan, where she gave birth to Shao Kang. He grew up in hiding, served as an official for friendly clans, and gathered loyal followers.

With their help Shao Kang defeated Han Zhuo and his sons and restored the Xia. Ancient writers called this the 'revival of Shao Kang'. The story comes from the Zuo Commentary and later texts and cannot be confirmed.
story_zh: 传统史书说，夏朝建立不久就险些灭亡。启的儿子太康只顾打猎，一次他到洛水对岸游猎，有穷氏首领、以善射闻名的后羿趁机阻断他的归路，夺取了政权。
后来后羿又被亲信寒浞杀死。寒浞篡位后四处追杀夏王族。一位怀孕的夏王后逃回娘家，生下了少康。少康在流亡中长大，在友好部族中当过小官，逐渐聚集起忠于夏朝的力量。
依靠这些力量，少康打败寒浞父子，恢复了夏朝统治，古人称之为“少康中兴”。这段故事出自《左传》等较晚的文献，无法得到证实。
shao-kang-restoration.why: It became the classic model of a fallen dynasty being restored by a lost heir, an image later rulers often invoked.
shao-kang-restoration.why_zh: 它成为“遗孤复国、王朝中兴”的经典范例，后世君主常以此自比。

people.name: Taikang
people.role: Xia king who lost the throne

people.name: Yi of Youqiong
people.role_zh: 夺取政权的有穷氏首领

story: The Qijia culture is named after Qijiaping in Guanghe county, Gansu, where the Swedish geologist Johan Gunnar Andersson found it in 1924. It spread across Gansu, Qinghai and Ningxia from about 2300 to 1500 BCE.

Qijia sites have produced some of the earliest metal objects in China: knives, awls, axes, rings and small mirrors made of copper and tin bronze. Many types resemble metalwork from the steppes of Central Asia, so scholars think metalworking reached China partly along routes through the northwest.
The Qijia people farmed millet and raised pigs, sheep and cattle. They also made fine jades and painted pottery, and their villages, such as Lajia, show settled life along the upper Yellow River.
story_zh: 齐家文化因甘肃广河县的齐家坪遗址而得名，1924年由瑞典地质学家安特生发现。它分布于甘肃、青海、宁夏一带，年代约为公元前2300年至前1500年。
齐家文化遗址出土了中国最早的一批金属器，包括用红铜和锡青铜制作的刀、锥、斧、指环和小铜镜。其中不少器型与中亚草原的金属器相似，因此学者认为冶金技术有一部分是经西北通道传入中国的。
齐家先民种植粟，饲养猪、羊和牛，还制作精美的玉器和彩陶。喇家等聚落反映了黄河上游的定居生活。
qijia-copper.why: Qijia metalwork helps explain how bronze technology reached the Central Plain, where Erlitou and then Shang made it the basis of state power.
qijia-copper.why_zh: 齐家文化的金属器有助于说明青铜技术如何传入中原；之后二里头和商人把它发展为国家权力的基础。

people.name: Johan Gunnar Andersson
people.role: Swedish geologist who identified the culture
people.role_zh: 发现该文化的瑞典地质学家

story: Jie, named Lü Gui, is listed as the last king of the Xia. The later histories describe him as strong enough to straighten iron hooks with his bare hands but cruel and wasteful as a ruler. They say he spent heavily on palaces, killed ministers who criticised him, and doted on his consort Moxi.

His people came to hate him. The Book of Documents records them comparing Jie to the sun, which he claimed would never die, and saying they would gladly die if only it would perish too. Jie also imprisoned Tang, the rising lord of Shang, at Xiatai, but later let him go.
Many of these stories copy those told about the last Shang king, so historians treat them with caution. Their message was that a ruler who abuses his people loses Heaven's support.
story_zh: 桀名履癸，是史书所列的夏朝最后一位君王。后世记载说他力大无穷，能徒手拉直铁钩，但治国残暴奢侈：大兴宫室，杀害进谏的大臣，宠爱妃子妺喜。
百姓对他深恶痛绝。据《尚书》记载，桀自比为永不陨落的太阳，百姓就指着太阳说：这个太阳什么时候灭亡？我们宁愿和你同归于尽。桀还曾把正在崛起的商族首领汤囚禁在夏台，后来又放了他。
这些故事有不少和商纣王的故事如出一辙，所以史学家对其持谨慎态度。它们想传达的是：虐待百姓的君主终将失去上天的支持。
jie-of-xia.why: Jie became the model 'bad last ruler' in Chinese history, used to justify the overthrow of a dynasty.
jie-of-xia.why_zh: 桀成为中国历史上“亡国之君”的典型，被用来说明推翻一个王朝的正当性。

people.name: Tang
people.role: Lord of Shang, later founder of the Shang
people.role_zh: 商族首领，后来的商朝开国君主

quote.en: When will this sun perish? We would die together with you!
quote.from: Book of Documents, Speech of Tang 尚书·汤誓
